note: Crafts of The Given Land/The Pattern Reach (concrete_abstract axis). THINGCRAFT is the concrete-pole craft of the Masons of the Given — only what can be touched is real; the world's great builders and its great skeptics. FORMCRAFT is the abstract-pole craft of the Figurists — pattern, symbol and idea, who hold matter to be the coarsest layer of the real. This is the axis the GM's own narrative REGISTER rides on (SNG-048): concrete places speak plainly, abstract places earn their poetry. Authored by Aevi, SNG-054.

abilities.name: Thingcraft
abilities.narrationHints: He puts his hand on the stone and the stone tells him the truth, because stone does not do anything else.
abilities.description: Know a thing's true weight, material, soundness and worth by touch — no lie of appearance survives your hand. The concrete-pole mastery, and the world's most stubborn skepticism.
abilities.notFor: Symbol, glamour, and argument (Formcraft's country); anything that requires believing in what cannot be weighed.

tree.name: Weighed Thing
tree.grants: Know a thing's true weight, material, soundness and worth by touch. No lie of appearance survives your hand.
tree.cannot: You must handle it. Tells you what it IS, not what it means.

tree.name: Set Stone
tree.grants: ⛔ SET A THING WHERE YOU PUT IT AND IT STAYS — a wall, a joint, a boundary, a claim, a door in its frame, a wheel on its axle. It resists levers, drift and quiet removal, and you know the instant it is worked at.
tree.cannot: One assembly at a time. Deliberate demolition still works.

tree.name: Denial
tree.grants: ⛔ DENY AN ABSTRACTION PURCHASE ON THE REAL. Illusion, glamour, symbol-working and figure-craft all fail inside the space you hold.
tree.cannot: The space you can reach. Physical force is unaffected.
tree._gainNote: ⛔ Denying abstraction purchase is a CONDITION the space now has, not a bigger space.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ THE AXIS'S WEAPON. r3 'denies an abstraction purchase on the real: illusion, glamour, SYMBOL-WORKING AND FIGURE all simply fail in your presence.' Authored with a TYPED soak (CCODE-83's mechanic) against `abstraction` — it is a ward against an entire opposing tradition, and it is TRANSPARENT to a sword.

abilities.name: Formcraft
abilities.narrationHints: They do the thing exactly as its own people do it, and slightly wrong in a way only those people would notice — the grammar is right and the accent is from nowhere.
abilities.description: Take the form of another craft — copy what you have seen worked, then what you have only heard of, then a form you have never encountered that arrives because you needed it.
abilities.notFor: Crafts nobody has ever worked; anything above tier IV; keeping a borrowed form — it is one use and it goes.

tree.name: Copied Form
tree.grants: ⛔ WORK A TIER I CRAFT YOU HAVE PERSONALLY SEEN WORKED, once. Not your tradition, not your power source — you read the form of what they did and take it.
tree.cannot: ⚠️ You must have WITNESSED it. Tier I only, one use, and it does not stay.

tree.name: Form from Report
tree.grants: ⛔ WORK A CRAFT UP TO TIER III THAT YOU HAVE ONLY HEARD DESCRIBED — a page in a text, a story told well enough, a witness who saw it. You take the form from the telling and work it once.
tree.cannot: ⛔ Someone must have described it in enough detail to have a form at all. A rumour of a craft is not a craft.
tree._grantsWas_SNG510: ⚠️ ADDS TIER AND SECONDHAND SOURCES. Up to TIER III, and you no longer need to have seen it — a described craft, a page in a text, a story told well enough carries the form.

tree.name: Form Out of Need
tree.grants: ⛔ WORK A CRAFT UP TO TIER IV WITH NO SOURCE AT ALL. The form arrives because the moment required it, and you work something you have never heard of and could not name afterwards.
tree.cannot: ⚠️ It comes when it comes. You do not choose which form arrives, only that you are open to one.
tree._grantsWas_SNG510: ⛔ ADDS THE UNKNOWN. Up to TIER IV, and you no longer need a source at all — the form arrives because the moment required it, and you work a craft you have never heard of and could not name afterwards.

⚠️ ERIK'S DESIGN: 'Perhaps Formcraft can be a DOPPELGANGER SKILL. r1 mimics a TIER I craft you've experienced. r2 mimics a craft up to TIER III that you've heard of, read about, or seen. r3 lets you mimic things you've NEVER EVEN HEARD ABOUT — the forms come to you out of NEED AND MEANING and you use it. abilities.name: Walking Figure
abilities.narrationHints: A chalked shape peels off the wall it was drawn on, goes where it was sent, and does the thing. It is not alive and it is not a servant; it is an instruction with edges.
abilities.description: Send a made figure to do a named thing in a place you are not — and, at its height, to judge the cases you did not foresee.
abilities.notFor: Places you have never seen; anything requiring a body; instructions you cannot state.

tree.name: Sent Figure
tree.grants: ⛔ SEND A FIGURE TO A PLACE YOU KNOW. It arrives and DOES ONE NAMED THING — bars a door, warns a person, marks a passage, holds a threshold — then ends.
tree.cannot: One thing, one place you have seen. It cannot improvise and it cannot fight.

tree.name: Figure That Stays
tree.grants: ⛔ SEND A FIGURE TO A PLACE YOU KNOW AND IT STAYS. The ward, the watch or the rule holds after you have gone — and you know when it fires and roughly what tripped it.
tree.cannot: It holds until broken or until the season turns. A determined breaker can still break the mark.
tree._grantsWas_SNG510: ⚠️ ADDS PERSISTENCE AND REPORT. The ward, the watch or the rule holds after you have gone — and you know when it fires and roughly what tripped it.

tree.name: Figure That Judges
tree.grants: ⛔ SEND A FIGURE THAT JUDGES. Give it INTENT rather than instruction — 'let no one through who is carrying steel' becomes 'let no one through who means her harm' — and it decides the cases you did not foresee.
tree.cannot: ⚠️ A FIGURE THAT INTERPRETS CAN INTERPRET WRONGLY, and it will not check with you first.

_treeWas.grants: The figure persists — it keeps meaning, keeps acting, keeps the ward or the rule in force after you have gone.
_treeWas.cannot: A standing figure is a rule nobody is supervising. It will apply itself to cases you never imagined.

_treeWas.name: The Figure That Learns
_treeWas.grants: The figure adapts its meaning to circumstance — it keeps doing what you MEANT even where you did not foresee. And a figure can be sent meaning harm: not a blow but a verdict walking, which arrives, finds the one it was addressed to, and enacts what was written into it.
_treeWas.cannot: A figure sent to harm is a figure that will do the SECOND thing you meant, not the first — the Figurists lose more of their own to this than to any enemy. abilities.name: Sound Repair
abilities.narrationHints: Not better. Sound. The thing as it was, correctly made, correctly set.

tree.cannot: You must be able to examine it. It repairs the material, never the meaning.

abilities.name: Set Word
abilities.narrationHints: A mason's word is set the way a stone is set. It does not shift.

tree.grants: ⛔ SAY THE PLAIN THING AND HAVE IT LAND. The practical fact that settles an argument by being undeniable — and your presence backs it: people make room, and those considering something reconsider.

tree.name: Word That Holds

tree._grantsWas: Move through a built environment at the speed its construction allows — the route that doesn't backtrack, the way that's already there in the material.
tree._cannotWas: Anything rank 3 adds — in any built structure, find or make the passage; BUILT structures only.

abilities.name: Keystone Blow
abilities.narrationHints: You do not batter the wall. You find the one stone the whole thing is truly resting on, and you strike THAT, and the wall discovers it was only ever an agreement between stones.
abilities.description: Find the one stone a structure is truly resting on and strike THAT, so the whole comes down for the cost of one blow. The Mason art of the keystone: to break well is to understand first.
abilities.notFor: It breaks the made, not the living or the grown — and it needs a real keystone; some things bear their load everywhere at once and have no single stone to strike. Read wrong and you have merely hit a wall.

tree.name: Keystone Blow
tree.grants: Find and strike a structure's single load-bearing point, bringing the whole down with one blow.
tree.cannot: It works only on made structures with a true keystone, it fails on distributed loads, and a thing brought down cannot be un-broken — you understood it in order to end it.

tree.grants: Where there is no true keystone, make one — a sequence of lesser strikes that manufactures the single load-bearing point, then takes it. Distributed loads no longer refuse you, and the scale rises from a structure to a span: a bridge, a gatehouse, a curtain wall.

abilities._descriptionWas: See the pattern beneath particulars — the first gift of the Pattern Reach.
abilities._revised: ⚠️ SNG-450. Erik: 'DON'T REMOVE r3 FROM PATTERN-SENSE — ADD SOMETHING TO IT.' ⛔ He is right that the fix for a weak rank is to make it do something, not to delete it. r3 was 'read the form of an event, a life, or a history — the shape it is completing', which is an observation. IT NOW ACTS ON THE FORM: name where the pattern must break, and act there.

abilities.name: Stone-Read
abilities.narrationHints: The material gives up its history under his palm.
abilities.description: Read a material's truth by touch — the first gift of the Given.
abilities.notFor: Reading meaning or intent; anything not physically present.

tree.name: Stone-Read
tree.grants: Know what a material truly is, and whether it is sound.
tree.cannot: Materials, not makers. It says the beam will fail; not who cut it badly.

tree.name: The Long Grain
tree.grants: Read a thing's history in its material — the stresses it took, the repairs, the day it nearly broke.
tree.cannot: History, not future. It reports what happened, not what happens next.

tree.name: The Given Word
tree.grants: The material of a whole structure is legible at once — every fault, every honest joint, every lie the builder told.
tree.cannot: Buildings you love turn out to be full of lies. The Masons say this is why they are hard to live with.

abilities.plainly: A investigate/explore action that reveals information or sets up a later action. Its strength is rated 3 out of 10, and lasts for about an hour Ranks: rank 2 deepens history; rank 3 extends perceptionDepth. Limit: materials, Not Makers — it says the beam will fail, not who cut it.

abilities.name: The True Figure
abilities.narrationHints: You see the shape a thing is actually making — the pattern under the mess, the geometry a crowd is unknowingly standing in, the figure a set of events describes. Once seen, it cannot be unseen.
abilities.description: Look at a scene, a record, a route, a crowd, a wound-pattern, and the craft names one thing: the element that does not fit, or the place where a piece is missing. The Figurists' first craft — pattern read rather than imposed.
abilities.notFor: Patterns that are not there (the craft returns nothing rather than obliging you); reading intent or meaning; anything genuinely random.

tree.name: The Shape Under It
tree.grants: Look at a scene, a set of records, a route, a crowd, a wound-pattern — and the craft NAMES ONE THING for you: the element that does not fit, or the place where a piece is missing and what shape it must be. One concrete answer, pointed at: this ledger entry, that stone, the fourth man, the room nobody uses.
tree.cannot: It shows the SHAPE, never the reason. And a genuinely chaotic thing has no figure — it returns nothing, which Figurists insist is a real answer.

tree.name: The Continued Line
tree.grants: Extend the figure — where the pattern goes next, what the missing piece must be, where the sixth one will be found.
tree.cannot: The extension is only as sound as the figure, and a partial pattern extends confidently and wrongly. Say which you have.

tree.name: The Whole Figure
tree.grants: The complete shape of a large thing — a campaign, a season of disappearances, a city's flow, a tradition's drift.
tree.cannot: ⚠ A LARGE FIGURE IS HARD TO STOP SEEING. Figurists at this rank read pattern into things that have none, and the craft cannot tell them apart from inside.

intensity.surge: the whole figure; IT IS HARD TO STOP SEEING, and the craft cannot tell you when there is none

_sng510: ⛔ SNG-510: grants rewritten SELF-CONTAINED. CCode measured that `progression.abilitiesForGM` sends ONLY the rank the player holds — `tree.find(t => t.rank === owned.level)` — so a grant opening 'ADDS RANGE. Throw it' referred to an r1 the model never sees. ⚠️ STRIPPING THE OPENER WAS NOT ENOUGH: 'it' and 'the same force' had no antecedent either. Each rank now names its own craft, its own effect and its own numbers.

_sng513: ⛔ SNG-513: `imposes` and `ongoingHarm` authored. Both readers were live and unfed — CCode named the fields rather than authoring content. ⚠️ `onCrit` IS ESCALATE: a crit imposes a DIFFERENT, stronger condition. `slain` is refused at all three doors — a craft is not a situation.
